title: Light as a Wave in a Vacuum Medium: A Visualizable Picture of Radiation, Relativity and Quantum Phenomena
content: Light is usually presented as an electromagnetic wave with no underlying substance, and students are left asking: a wave of what? This article explores an older and more visual answer. Space is filled with a physical, elastic medium whose permittivity and permeability, the measured constants of the vacuum, set the speed of light. Using J. J. Thomson’s geometric construction, an accelerated charge leaves a kink in the field lines that detaches as an expanding shell of transverse field. The   radiation field and the   pattern follow from similar triangles, Larmor’s formula follows from the energy in the shell, and the electric and magnetic parts of the pulse carry equal energy and sustain each other as it travels. Maxwell’s equations are given a mechanical reading, with a rotationally elastic model that has the same equations. Following Lorentz and Poincaré, length contraction and time dilation appear as physical effects of motion through the medium, and the Michelson–Morley null result is what such a medium predicts. This picture is empirically equivalent to special relativity. The central claim is that the photoelectric effect, the Compton effect and blackbody radiation can be accounted for with light as a classical wave in the medium, the quantization belonging to the matter, the electron or the wall resonators, and not to the light. The article also discusses refraction and dispersion, signals in conductors, superconductivity and Bose condensation, gravity as a graded-index lens, and entanglement as a single non-separable pattern. It states which parts are standard results, interpretations and hypotheses. The medium has not been detected directly, non-classical light remains the main challenge to a wave-only account, and the open problems and possible tests are listed.
